Chasing hot themes, hypergrowth stocks or multibaggers? Why Rajeev Thakkar of PPFAS Mutual Fund prefers fundamentals
articles.summary: In a market where investors are often drawn to hot themes, hypergrowth stocks and the prospect of multibagger returns, PPFAS Mutual Fund CIO and Director Rajeev Thakkar reiterates the importance of staying focused on fundamentals rather than chasing popular investment trends.During its 13th Unitholders’ Meet on Saturday, Thakkar explained why PPFAS does not actively chase companies expected to become 10-baggers, 20-baggers or even 100-baggers. He said the fund house's investment decisions are guided by the quality of a business, its financial performance and the valuation at which it is available rather than the excitement surrounding a particular sector or investment theme.CIO @RajeevThakkar reiterates why we steer clear of "hot themes" and stick to fundamentals.#PPFASAGM https://t.co/5JkZYQkyGC— PPFAS (@PPFAS) November 21, 2026Also Read | Capitalmind Flexi Cap Fund increases stake in MCX, Radico Khaitan, 9 others, makes exit from Bajaj Auto and 8 moreTo illustrate his point, Thakkar compared Coal India, which is part of the fund house's portfolio, with a popular company operating in a hot investment theme that PPFAS Mutual Fund does not own. He clarified that the comparison was not intended to criticise the other company but to demonstrate why the price investors pay for growth matters.Coal India reported revenue of Rs 1.71 lakh crore and profits of over Rs 33,000 crore, compared with Rs 78,000 crore in revenue and less than Rs 500 crore in profits for the other company. While Coal India offered a 6.6% dividend yield and traded at a PE of around 7, the other company paid no dividends and traded at a PE of over 700.Thakkar acknowledged that the hot-theme company could grow its business and profits in the coming years. However, he questioned how long it could take for a company earning less than Rs 500 crore to reach the profit levels of a business already generating more than Rs 33,000 crore.Thakkar also cited examples of past investment themes to explain why investors should be careful about paying excessive valuations for companies with strong growth prospects.He referred to a company that had tripled its profits over five years, but whose stock price had declined by around one-third. The reason, he explained, was that the starting valuation was too high and investors had built in expectations of substantial future growth.Despite the sharp correction and the threefold increase in profits, the stock was still trading at a PE multiple of more than 70. This illustrated why even a well-managed company with promising business prospects may not necessarily turn out to be a good investment if investors pay too much for it.Thakkar also challenged the notion that investors should always prefer companies with high earnings growth.He explained that even a company with zero earnings growth could be an attractive investment if it generated cash flows equivalent to its earnings and distributed all its profits to shareholders as dividends.Using a theoretical example, he said a stock trading at five times its earnings and distributing all its profits as dividends would offer a 20% dividend yield. Even if its earnings remained unchanged for 25 years, he would be comfortable owning such a business because of the cash flows it generated for shareholders.He said investment decisions should not be based solely on earnings multiples or growth rates. Investors need to consider both the growth potential of a business and whether they are paying a reasonable valuation for it.Thakkar said there are several misconceptions about what equity fund managers should and should not do. He clarified that the investment team does not attempt to predict quarterly earnings surprises, changes in interest rates, foreign portfolio investor (FPI) flows, geopolitical developments or the outcome of political events. These factors can influence stock prices but are largely outside the control of fund managers.Thakkar also addressed investor concerns about artificial intelligence (AI), the capital expenditure cycle and the sustainability of investments made by global technology companies.He acknowledged that AI is a significant technological development and could create substantial opportunities. However, he also cautioned that excessive capital expenditure in the sector could lead to disruptions over the next two to three years.Also Read | Silver ETFs crash over 56% from January peak. Should investors buy, hold or exit?Thakkar also pointed out that the availability of open-source and open-weight AI models could change the competitive landscape. While these models may not match the most advanced frontier models in every aspect, they could be sufficient for several everyday business applications.Therefore, the fund house believes that investing in companies with multiple established revenue streams can offer a different risk profile compared with businesses whose success depends largely on a single AI model or emerging business.Thakkar also addressed concerns about the fund house's investments in Indian IT services companies, including TCS, Infosys and HCL Technologies. He clarified that these stocks accounted for less than 10% of the portfolio and that the fund house was not taking an excessively large exposure to the sector.Responding to the argument that AI could make traditional software services businesses obsolete, he said market narratives often become exaggerated and can create investment opportunities.Commenting on why PPFAS Mutual Fund is selective about mid-cap and small-cap stocks, Thakkar said the fund house does not have anything against small-cap or mid-cap stocks and would invest in them when valuations become attractive. However, it would remain selective rather than buying companies simply because they belong to a particular market-cap segment or are part of a popular theme.He pointed out that several companies held by the fund house, including REITs and natural gas businesses, fall within the mid-cap space. He added that small-cap returns can look very attractive when investors enter at the right time, but can be disappointing during other market cycles. He also noted that the small-cap premium has been declining globally..Addressing another frequently discussed concern among unitholders, Thakkar shared his views on whether a mutual fund's size affects its ability to generate returns.He said he had used several AI tools to examine the relationship between fund size and performance across different mutual fund categories. According to the findings he shared, fund size has a relatively limited impact on large-cap and flexi-cap funds, with larger funds having performed better in the analysis. The impact of size is more relevant in the small-cap category.He also highlighted the importance of expense ratios, pointing out that larger funds typically have lower expense ratios, which can benefit investors. The pace at which a fund's assets under management (AUM) grow is another important factor, rather than just its absolute size.Also Read | NFO Insight: Bajaj Finserv Business Cycle Fund is open for subscription. Should investors bet on changing economic cycles?Thakkar added that a fund manager could underperform even with a much smaller AUM, indicating that fund size alone does not determine investment performance.(Disclaimer: Recommendations, suggestions, views and opinions given by the experts are their own. articles.title: From record highs to a brutal rout: What is behind the meltdown in gold and silver?
articles.summary: Gold and silver are witnessing a sharp reversal after their spectacular rally, with a strengthening US dollar, increasingly hawkish Federal Reserve expectations and investor liquidations triggering a sustained sell-off across precious metals.The correction has been particularly severe in silver, which has plunged 41% over the past six months, compared with a 19% decline in gold. The selling has accelerated over the past month, with silver losing 19% and gold falling 9%.Spot gold was quoted at $3,524.80 an ounce, down 4.33%, while spot silver traded at $40.99 an ounce, declining around 7%.Why are gold and silver falling?A major trigger for gold's latest decline has been the changing outlook for US monetary policy, with increasingly hawkish signals from Federal Reserve policymakers strengthening expectations of further interest-rate increases.According to Reuters, comments from US Federal Reserve policymakers have reinforced the hawkish tone of the Federal Open Market Committee's October meeting. Philadelphia Fed President Anna Paulson flagged inflation risks that could warrant another interest-rate increase, strengthening expectations that US borrowing costs could rise further.Markets are pricing in a 96% probability of a 25-basis-point US rate hike in December, according to the CME FedWatch tool.Minutes of the Fed's October 27-28 meeting, released on Wednesday, also highlighted spolicymakers' concerns about persistent inflation pressures. Although the central bank left interest rates unchanged, some participants supported a 25-basis-point increase at the October meeting, while a couple flagged the possibility of a larger increase in December.Artificial intelligence-related demand also featured in the discussions, with policymakers identifying it as a material source of inflation risk.The changing interest-rate outlook has strengthened the US dollar, which has climbed to a 19-month high. A stronger dollar makes dollar-denominated bullion more expensive for buyers using other currencies, adding to the pressure on prices.Higher interest rates also increase the opportunity cost of holding gold, which does not generate interest income, making yield-bearing assets relatively more attractive.Gold struggles to find safe-haven supportThe latest decline has come despite renewed tensions in the Middle East. Even as gold has entered increasingly oversold territory, bullion has struggled to attract buying, with the dollar's strength, rising yield expectations and investor liquidations outweighing its traditional safe-haven appeal.On Friday, gold fell to $3,513.54 an ounce, its lowest level since September 4, 2025.Bullion had lost around 8% during the week, putting it on course for its steepest weekly decline in eight months. US gold futures for December delivery fell 2.7% to $3,587.90 an ounce.The ongoing sell-off in artificial intelligence-related equities has also contributed to the pressure, with some investors reportedly liquidating gold positions to cover losses elsewhere in their portfolios.Tony Sage, CEO of Critical Metals, said gold was under renewed pressure from hawkish Federal Reserve expectations, which were lifting real yields and the US dollar while increasing the opportunity cost of holding a non-yielding asset."The ongoing AI-related equity selloff is also prompting some forced liquidations of gold positions to cover losses elsewhere," Sage said.Why has silver fallen more sharply than gold?Silver's 41% decline over six months, against gold's 19% fall, highlights the greater volatility of the white metal.According to Sage, silver, platinum and palladium are declining alongside gold primarily because of the same macroeconomic drivers. However, silver's typically higher volatility has amplified the market movement."Silver, platinum and palladium are declining in tandem with gold primarily because of the same macro drivers. Silver is typically more volatile and has amplified the move this week," Sage said.He added that platinum and palladium were also sensitive to growth concerns accompanying tighter monetary policy.Investment demand remains an important supportThe accumulation strategy comes even as the World Gold Council expects investment demand to remain the leading driver of growth in gold demand in 2026.However, the council has lowered its forecast for the increase in average annual gold demand from 400 tonnes to 200 tonnes year-on-year.Gold ETF inflows have exceeded expectations, while demand for bars and coins has remained relatively resilient, although it slowed considerably in the second half of the year.ETF inflows during the third quarter were particularly notable, coming despite a sharp rise in bond yields, a stronger US dollar and a decline in the Geopolitical Risk Index.The data suggests that concerns around fiscal conditions and broader economic uncertainty have partly offset the higher opportunity cost of holding gold.Gold finds support at $3,500; silver at $38-$39Anindya Banerjee, Head of Commodity, Currency and Rate Derivatives at Kotak Neo, said $3,500 remains the first important support level for gold, within a broader support zone of $3,400-$3,500."We would look for a daily hammer or doji in that area, followed by buying in the next session. That would be the first evidence that the market is absorbing the selling. Until then, the trend remains down," Banerjee said.For silver, the next major support zone is seen at $38-$39 an ounce. Banerjee said the metal would also need a similar reversal signal to indicate that selling pressure was easing.The next move in precious metals will depend on the interplay between US monetary policy, currency movements and global demand. Gold could find support from safe-haven buying, geopolitical uncertainty and central-bank purchases, while silver's longer-term prospects could benefit from industrial demand and persistent supply deficits.Disclosure: This article has been written by Kumar Gaurav, who is not a Sebi-registered Research Analyst or an Investment Adviser. The stock then posted a steep decline on its second day of trading.The IPO, together with Nvidia’s quarterly earnings report, failed to ease concerns about stretched valuations and the enormous sums being invested in AI infrastructure.“Nvidia reported what might have been one of the greatest quarters in corporate earnings history; they did everything right,” said Chuck Carlson, chief executive officer at Horizon Investment Services, as per Reuters' report.“A lot of people, myself included, were looking to the Anthropic debut to some extent as a clearing event, and it wasn’t.”The Philadelphia Semiconductor Index, which had been a major driver of the broader market’s advance, tumbled as the once-crowded chip trade continued to unwind.Amazon and Meta Platforms were among the hyperscalers that suffered heavy losses, while AI cloud-computing companies CoreWeave and Nebius also fell sharply.The technology rout encouraged investors to move into traditionally defensive areas, including consumer staples and healthcare.Inflation and Fed policy in focusFederal Reserve Governor Lisa Cook said the central bank’s policy rate was not sufficiently high to address elevated inflation.Traders were pricing in a near-certain 25-basis-point interest-rate increase at the Fed’s December meeting, according to CME Group’s FedWatch tool.A University of Michigan survey showed an improvement in consumer sentiment following the election.Investors will turn next week to the personal consumption expenditures report, which includes the Fed’s preferred inflation measure, for further guidance on monetary policy after October inflation exceeded expectations.Among individual stocks, Intuit fell after lowering its annual revenue-growth forecast and agreeing to sell Mailchimp to Bending Spoons for about $3.68 billion. The vaccine has been developed by the ICAR-National Institute of High Security Animal Diseases in Bhopal, officials from the Union Agriculture Ministry said.
This is the first-of-its-kind vaccine developed in India against the H5N1 virus of Clade 2.3.2.1a of the highly pathogenic avian influenza (HPAI), they said.
Speaking on the occasion, Chouhan said, "This vaccine is an example of India's self-reliance."
HPAI, commonly known as bird flu, is a serious disease affecting chickens and other birds. Outbreaks can result in almost 100 per cent mortality among infected birds.
Besides the Union Agriculture Minister, Madhya Pradesh Sports and Youth Welfare and Cooperatives Minister Vishwas Sarang and Bhopal BJP MP Alok Sharma, among others, were also present at the ceremony held here.

India levies 20% on short-term and 12.5% on long-term gains, which works out to roughly 13% to 21.84% for FPIs once surcharge and cess are included. Most major global markets, including the US, UK, Singapore, Hong Kong, Germany and the UAE, charge no capital gains tax on foreign investors. Our guests weigh in on whether this gap is hurting FPI sentiment, how the tax burden compares between FPIs and local investors, and whether STT and capital gains tax together amount to double taxation of equities. They also discuss the case for abolishing capital gains tax, the options the government has to rationalise it, and whether the Finance Minister could announce relief in the upcoming Budget.

articles.title: UK, EU hold rare summit to mend Brexit damage
articles.summary: BRUSSELS - A decade after the people of Britain voted to leave the European Union, top EU officials are meeting with Prime Minister Andy Burnham on Friday, looking to mend more fences, and just perhaps, to pave the way for them to get back together.Burnham is scheduled to hold just under an hour of talks in Brussels with European Council President Antonio Costa and European Commission President Ursula von der Leyen. Then they'll all meet in a plenary session with U.K. government ministers and European commissioners.Burnham has described the rare EU-U.K. summit - only the second since Britain became the first country to leave the world's biggest trading bloc - as a step toward undoing a decade of damage caused by the divorce."The Brexit we were given has not worked. We have lost more than we gained," he said this week.Burnham has said all options should be on the table for future relations, including rejoining the now-27-nation bloc. But he's stressed that reversing Brexit is just one possible outcome, and far from imminent. It would need the backing not just of British voters, but the unanimous support of a mistrustful EU. Still, he has broken a long political code of silence on the option of rejoining.Ahead of the meeting, von der Leyen said she wanted it to be "a summit of ambition and concrete results. More opportunities for young people. Easier agrifood trade. And a stronger cooperation on economic security."Burnham pitched the package of agreements expected to be signed Friday as a way of "cutting costs, keeping prices down in the supermarkets and creating opportunities for young people."He said "a closer partnership with Europe is good for working people, good for Britain and good for Europe."The deals are set to include an agreement for up to 100,000 young adults from Britain to live and work in EU countries for up to three years, and the same number of Europeans to come to the U.K.There will also be an emissions trading agreement and a deal to remove checks on food and agricultural products that will make things cheaper and easier for British exporters to Europe. Burnham says the deals could add a modest 0.4% to Britain's economy.To get the deals, the U.K. must accept some EU rules and standards that it has no role in setting. Supporters of Brexit say that undermines Britain's independence."I'm afraid that the great Brexit debate has just started again," Reform UK leader Nigel Farage told the BBC. He said "it's perfectly clear that this very, very soon becomes a debate about: do we rejoin or do we stay out?"The war in Ukraine, and the U.K.'s military strength, are drawing the two back together, and the summit provides the EU with an opportunity to discuss stronger cooperation on security and defense, as well as efforts to restrict irregular migration."Our security and prosperity are closely intertwined, making a strong partnership between us essential," Costa said ahead of the meeting. "By deepening our cooperation, we can strengthen our ability to address the challenges of our time, strengthen our resilience and promote stability in Europe and beyond."Nevertheless, feelings remain raw, and EU officials have been reluctant to encourage talk of the U.K. rejoining. They are weary from the shifting demands of seven British prime ministers over the last decade and want real clarity about the country's intentions.Ireland's ambassador in London, Sonja Hyland, said that when Britain voted for Brexit, "there was a lack of clarity as to exactly what that meant." If Britain wants to reopen negotiations, she said, it must "make a clear decision as to what it wants."

articles.summary:

The Protect Our Neighbours Act, introduced by Congressman John Garamendi, draws inspiration from the deportation of Harjit Kaur, a resident of the San Francisco Bay Area, by the Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) last year.

articles.title: Centre notifies revised disability assessment norms for 8 categories
articles.summary:
The Centre has notified revised guidelines for assessing eight categories of specified disabilities under the Rights of Persons with Disabilities Act, 2016, replacing the norms issued in March 2024.
The guidelines, issued by the Department of Empowerment of Persons with Disabilities on November 18, cover locomotor disability, visual impairment, hearing impairment and speech and language disability, specific learning disability, intellectual disability and autism spectrum disorder, mental illness, blood disorder, multiple disorder and chronic neurological disorder.
For locomotor disabilities, assessment of the upper extremities covers the arm and hand, including range of motion, muscle strength, coordinated activities, prehension and sensation.
Conditions covered include amputation, cerebral palsy, leprosy-cured persons, dwarfism, muscular dystrophy and spinal deformities.
Except in cases of amputation, temporary disability certificates will be issued after six months of symptoms. .

articles.title: India, Japan deepen defence & economic ties
articles.summary: New Delhi: India and Japan have agreed to deepen collaboration across defence, economic security, and critical technologies, while unveiling a joint logo to mark 75 years of diplomatic relations, as External Affairs Minister S Jaishankar concluded his three-day official visit to Japan on Friday.According to the Ministry of External Affairs, during the November 18-20 visit, Jaishankar participated in the fourth India-Japan Foreign and Defence Ministerial Dialogue (2+2) alongside Defence Minister Rajnath Singh and their Japanese counterparts, Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi and Defence Minister Shinjiro Koizumi.According to an official release by the MEA, the ministers reaffirmed their commitment to a free, open, and rules-based Indo-Pacific and agreed to expand cooperation in defence exercises, defence manufacturing, maritime security, cybersecurity, and space. Both sides welcomed the signing of a Letter of Intent allowing the Japan Self-Defence Forces to utilise firing ranges in India, agreed to advance project-based economic security cooperation in strategic sectors, and reiterated their resolve to combat terrorism in all its forms. A joint statement was issued following the dialogue.Jaishankar also held the 19th Foreign Ministers' Strategic Dialogue (FMSD) with Japanese Foreign Minister Toshimitsu Motegi. The MEA stated that both leaders emphasised the growing significance of resilient supply chains and economic security, exploring deeper partnerships in critical and emerging technologies, semiconductors, critical minerals, artificial intelligence, digital public infrastructure, telecommunications, and advanced manufacturing.Reviewing bilateral commercial ties, the two ministers discussed efforts to boost Japanese investment in India and expand collaboration in mobility, infrastructure, and logistics. They also underscored people-to-people ties as a core pillar of the relationship, reaffirming their commitment to implementing the Action Plan for India-Japan Human Resource Exchange alongside discussions on regional Indo-Pacific issues and global developments.Looking ahead to 2027, which marks the 75th anniversary of diplomatic relations between New Delhi and Tokyo, Jaishankar and Motegi reviewed preparations for upcoming commemorative events and jointly unveiled the 75th Anniversary Joint Logo symbolising the India-Japan Special Strategic and Global Partnership.During his stay in Tokyo, Jaishankar also met with former Japanese Prime Minister and current Japan-India Association (JIA) Chairman Fumio Kishida, as well as Liberal Democratic Party Vice President Taro Aso. Additionally, he addressed the 3rd Raisina Tokyo conference, highlighting India's economic transformation, expanding global footprint, and new avenues for bilateral collaboration."EAM's visit to Japan reaffirmed the shared resolve of both countries to advance their partnership and contribute jointly to peace, stability and prosperity in the Indo-Pacific and beyond," the MEA said.

articles.title: NMC seeks to drop equal-licence requirement for foreign medical graduates
articles.summary:
The National Medical Commission (NMC) has proposed amending rules governing foreign medical graduates, seeking to remove the requirement that their licence to practise medicine in the country where they obtained their medical degree must be on par with the licence granted to citizens of that country.
Under the proposed amendment, a foreign medical graduate would need to be registered with the respective professional regulatory body in the country where the medical degree was awarded.
The change has been proposed in sub-clause (b) of Clause 4 of the National Medical Commission (Foreign Medical Graduate Licentiate) Regulations, 2021.
